title: Practice: The family of стать (переста́ть, установи́ть)

exercises.why: **стало** — стать (perfective): to stand (in a certain location or near someone or something); to begin; (in the negative) to be willing, to be going (used to express a determined negative attitude); to cost.

exercises.why: From Wiktionary: стать — to stand (in a certain location or near someone or something); переста́ть — to stop, to cease, to quit; установи́ть — to install, to place, to mount; приста́ть — to stick, to adhere.
**установить** — установи́ть (perfective): to install, to place, to mount; to establish, to set; to determine, to fix, to ascertain. Wiktionary: у- + -станови́ть.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: Those who live in glass houses should not throw stones.
exercises.ru: Живущим в стеклянных домах не ___ бросаться камнями.
exercises.why: **пристало** — приста́ть (perfective): to stick, to adhere; (colloquial) to bother, to pester. Wiktionary: при- + стать.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: The time may come when people will have used up all the oil.
exercises.ru: Может ___, что люди израсходуют всю нефть на Земле.
exercises.why: **статься** — ста́ться (perfective): to become, to happen. Wiktionary: ста́ть + -ся.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: The witnesses appeared before the judge.
exercises.why: **предстали** — предста́ть (perfective): to appear (before). Wiktionary: пред- + стать.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: Tom is due to be arraigned on October 20th.
exercises.why: **предстать** — предста́ть (perfective): to appear (before). Wiktionary: пред- + стать.
